text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. - - - -
-- Vietnam's least-developed area in the northern mountains will receive as much as $3.5 billion worth of development projects for the next five years.

-- A National Control Committee on socio-economic development in the Central Highlands has been established. The committee will cooperate with relevant ministries, agencies and the Central Highlands' Provincial People's Committees.

-- The national AIDS committee reports there were 4,344 HIV carriers by mid-September. The committee said the increasing numbers of HIV and AIDS carriers in Vietnam were mostly diagnosed among drug addicts and prostitutes.
-- The Prime Minister of Norway, Gro Harlem Brundland, will become the first Norwegian head of state to visit Vietnam since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 1971.
-- Vietnam's steel sector has produced over 646,000 tonnes of rolled steel so far this year.
-- Vietnam's paper industry now has 15,000 tonnes of paper stockpiled due to a 6.9-percent rise in production in the first nine months of this year compared with the same period of 1995. - - - -
-- The Southern Steel Company produced 209,387 tonnes of steel in the first nine months of this year, up 38 percent from the same period of last year.
-- Japan's Fujita company was chosen to take part in a $35.8 million project to upgrade part of the highway linking Hanoi and the port of Haiphong, which started on Monday.
-- Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced one to death and two to life imprisonment in a banking fraud case on Monday. - - - -
-- The government asked Mekong Delta provinces to take urgent measures to protect people and property from flooding.
-- Hanoi's police force arrested 54 and charged six youngsters for involvement in an illegal motor race. - - - -
-- The Standing Committee of Hanoi's Communist Party cell held a meeting to discuss five-year plans to develop the city.
-- Vietnam Airlines carried more than 1.8 million passengers and 31,600 tonnes of cargo in the first nine months of this year. - - - -
